answers.answer: 1) Four players select 3 Escape Pod tokens. 2) Place the lowest-numbered pod in Section A, the next in B, then alternate A/B. 3) All pods start Locked side up. 4) The Intruder bag contains 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player (so 7 Adults for four players).
answers.evidence: Setup steps 7 and 10: ‘3 for 3–4 players’; ‘lowest-numbered pod in Section A…then alternate A/B’; ‘All pods start with their Locked side’; bag token list and ‘1 additional Adult per player.’

answers.answer: 1) Remove Objective cards showing a player count higher than the actual player count from both Corporate and Personal decks. 2) Shuffle the decks separately and deal each player 1 Corporate and 1 Personal Objective, kept hidden. 3) At the First Encounter—the first time any Intruder miniature appears—each player chooses 1 of their 2 Objectives and removes the other face down, unseen. 4) The rejected card is removed from the game; players may never look at others’ removed Objectives. 5) Eggs do not trigger this choice because Eggs are not Intruders.
answers.evidence: Setup step 16; Special Rules, ‘First Encounter’: choose 1 of 2 and remove the other face down; ‘Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this.’

answers.answer: 1) Discard the Action card being played and the two additional Action cards required by its printed cost of 2. 2) The two Contamination cards cannot pay any Action cost and are not substituted. 3) If the Action card has sections separated by OR, choose one section/effect.
answers.evidence: Actions: ‘discard that card face up and pay its cost by discarding the required number of additional Action cards’; ‘Contamination cards…can never be discarded to pay’; ‘If a card has two sections separated by OR, choose one.’

answers.answer: 1) They suffer 1 Light Wound after finishing their own round, so after the one Action and pass. 2) Once passed, they may take no further Actions that Player Phase. 3) When passing, they may discard any number of cards from their hand. 4) Later players’ rounds do not make them take Fire damage again; the rule applies at the end of their own round, and passing players take it once at that point and no more that turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Player rounds: ‘ends their round in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Light Wound’; ‘Once you pass you may perform NO further Actions’; passing allows discarding any number; ‘passing players take it once at the end of their round and no more that turn.’

answers.answer: 1) On entering an unexplored Room, flip its tile face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token. 2) Set the Item count by rotating the Room tile until the token’s number faces the board’s Item Counter symbol; do not set a count for the Nest or Room Covered In Slime. 3) Resolve the token effect, then remove the token from the game into the box. 4) If the destination is empty, normally make a Noise roll; a Silence Exploration effect suppresses that roll, and a Danger effect also suppresses it and resolves Danger instead. 5) On a Silence Noise result, place no marker; if the Character has Slime, treat Silence as Danger. 6) On Danger, all eligible neighboring Intruders move in; if none are eligible, place Noise in every connected Corridor without a marker. 7) If any Character or Intruder is already in the entered Room, do not roll Noise.
answers.evidence: Movement, Rooms, and Corridors; Exploration tokens; Noise roll: flip/reveal, set count, resolve effect, remove token; ‘never roll for Noise when moving into a Room containing another Character or an Intruder’; Silence and Danger rules.

answers.answer: 1) Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards. 2) Instead of rolling Noise after moving, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination Room. 3) It is forbidden if all Corridors connected to the destination already have Noise markers, and it cannot be used in Combat. 4) Closed Doors block Character Movement, so they cannot be crossed. 5) A miniature cannot stop in a Corridor; characters and Intruders may occupy only Rooms.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions, Careful Movement; Movement, Rooms, and Corridors: ‘Closed Door blocks…Movement’ and ‘no one may ever stop in a Corridor.’

answers.answer: 1) The numbered Noise result instructs placement in a Corridor that already has Noise, so resolve an Encounter. 2) At the start of the Encounter, discard all Noise markers in Corridors connected to the Room, including the Technical Corridors space if connected. 3) Draw an Intruder token; if it is non-Blank, place its matching miniature and keep that token aside outside the bag. 4) Compare the token number with the triggering player’s hand size counting Action and Contamination cards; fewer cards than the number causes a Surprise Attack against the triggering Character. 5) Contamination cards count for this comparison, though they cannot pay Action costs. 6) If the drawn token is Blank, place Noise in each connected Corridor and return the Blank to the bag; if it was the last token in the bag, add an Adult token if available. No miniature or Surprise Attack results from Blank.
answers.evidence: Noise roll; Technical Corridors; Special Rules, Encounters and ‘Blank token in an Encounter’; Player Reference, Encounter: clear connected Noise including Technical Corridors; hand comparison includes Contamination.

answers.answer: 1) Danger moves all neighboring Intruders that are not in Combat with any Character into the Room. 2) If none are eligible (none neighboring or all are in Combat), place a Noise marker in each connected Corridor that lacks one. 3) Merely moving an Intruder into a Room with a Character is not an Encounter; the Character and Intruder are simply in Combat. 4) Slime changes any Silence result, from a Noise roll or Exploration token, into Danger.
answers.evidence: Noise roll, Danger; Special Rules, Encounters: an Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is NOT an Encounter; Slime marker rule.

answers.answer: 1) In an Encounter, a Blank places a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room, then returns to the bag; the Encounter ends without a miniature appearing. 2) If the Blank was the last token in the bag, add 1 Adult token if one is available. 3) In bag development, a Blank adds 1 Adult token to the bag if one is available, then the Blank itself returns to the bag; the summary does not describe restoring connected Noise in bag development.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, ‘Blank token in an Encounter’; Turn Structure, Event Phase, Intruder bag development: ‘Blank — add 1 Adult Intruder token to the bag… Return the Blank token to the bag.’

answers.answer: 1) Both Intruders stay in the Room; they destroy the Closed Door simultaneously. 2) The Door is left lying, which means Destroyed: movement is allowed through it, and it cannot be Closed again (except by the Plasma Torch Item). 3) A Noise-triggered Intruder appearance through that Corridor is not blocked by a Closed Door; it appears regardless of the Door.
answers.evidence: Fire, Malfunction, Doors, Slime and Noise markers: multiple Intruders from the same Room destroy a Closed Door simultaneously and all stay put; destroyed doors cannot be closed again except with Plasma Torch; Noise-caused appearance ignores Closed Door.

answers.answer: 1) The Intruder disappears into the ducts and its miniature is removed from the board. 2) Discard all Injury markers on it. 3) Return its token to the Intruder bag. 4) The Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space remains. 5) Characters normally cannot use Technical Corridors; the Mechanic’s Technical Corridors Action card and Technical Corridor Plans Item are exceptions. 6) Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.
answers.evidence: Technical Corridors: Intruder disappears, injuries discarded, token returned, Noise marker NOT removed; Characters’ exceptions; ‘Door tokens can never be placed’ there.

answers.answer: 1) Both Shoot and Melee are Basic Actions costing 1 Action card. 2) Shoot requires a Weapon in Hand with Ammo; choose one Intruder in your Room, discard 1 Ammo, and roll the Combat die. A blank misses without a wound penalty. 3) Melee targets one Intruder in your Room; draw a Contamination card and put it on top of your Action discard pile before rolling. 4) A Melee miss gives the Character 1 Serious Wound. 5) A two-hit result deals 2 Injuries when Shooting (before Weapon modifications), but only 1 Injury in Melee.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions; Special Rules, Combat, Shoot and Melee Attack; Contamination cards: gains go on top of Action discard pile.

answers.answer: 1) A Larva dies at 1 Injury. 2) For an Adult, draw 1 Intruder Attack card and compare its blood value to the Intruder’s Injury markers: blood equal to or lower than Injuries means it dies. 3) For a Queen, draw 2 cards, add their blood values, and compare the total to its Injury markers the same way. 4) A Carcass is placed for any dead Intruder except a Larva. 5) If any card drawn for the Queen’s Injury Effect shows the Retreat arrow, resolve retreat instead of a numerical death result: draw an Event card and move the Intruder through the Corridor given by its movement section, then discard that Event card.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, ‘Intruder Injuries and death’ and ‘Intruder Retreat’: Larva/Egg die at 1; Adult uses one blood value; Queen uses sum of two; carcass except Larvae; Queen retreats if either card has Retreat.

answers.answer: 1) Before moving, resolve one separate Intruder Attack for each of the two Intruders in the Room. 2) Escape attacks target the escaper. 3) If the Character dies, their Corpse stays in the Room they tried to Escape from. 4) If they survive, move into the neighboring unexplored Room; reveal and resolve the Room and Exploration token, then make a Noise roll if the destination is empty, following the normal entry rules.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Character Escape: one Intruder Attack per Intruder before moving; if survive complete move with Noise if empty and explore normally; if die Corpse remains in source Room. Movement, Rooms, and Corridors gives entry order: reveal/resolve unexplored Room first, then Noise roll if empty.

answers.answer: 1) With several Characters in the Room, target the one whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand; ties go to the Character with the First Player token, or the next player in turn order. 2) Draw an Intruder Attack card; it hits if its symbol matches the attacking Intruder type, otherwise it misses. 3) A Larva does not draw an Attack card: remove its miniature and place it on the target’s Character board, and the target gains 1 Contamination card. 4) That Contamination card is placed on top of the target’s Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Intruder Attack and Infest (Larva attack); Contamination cards: placed on top of Action discard pile.

answers.answer: 1) Dressing a Serious Wound does not prevent death from a further Wound when the Character already has 3 Serious Wounds; dressing only ignores the card’s effect. 2) Otherwise, a third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and becomes a Serious Wound. 3) Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies. 4) On death, place a Character Corpse token in the Room as a Character Corpse Object and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: Character Wounds and death: dressing does not prevent death with 3 Serious Wounds; third Light Wound converts to Serious; Heal effects; death places Corpse token and drops all Heavy Objects in the Room.

answers.answer: 1) Canteen and Shower Room scan only Contamination cards in the Character’s hand. They remove all non-Infected cards; an Infected result places a Larva on the Character’s board (if one is already there, the Character dies and a Creeper appears in the Room). 2) Surgery scans all the Character’s Contamination cards in their deck, hand, and discard pile; removes all Infected ones and removes a Larva from the board if present. 3) Surgery then causes 1 Light Wound, automatically passes the Character for the rest of the Player Phase, and shuffles all their cards (including their entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into their Action deck; their hand stays empty until next turn.
answers.evidence: Canteen and Shower Room actions; Surgery Room Action: scans all zones, removes Infected and Larva, then Light Wound, automatic pass and shuffle.

answers.answer: 1) Shoot or Melee against uncarried Eggs: each Injury destroys one Egg. 2) A missed Egg Melee waives both the normal Contamination card and the Serious Wound. Whether a successful Egg Melee gives Contamination is unsupported by the summary, which says the manual does not uniquely settle it. 3) A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs; a Molotov Cocktail destroys 1. 4) A Fire marker in a Room with uncarried Eggs destroys 1 during each Fire Damage step. 5) Make a Noise roll after every single attempt to destroy an Egg. 6) When no Eggs remain, the Nest is destroyed and marked with 1 Injury marker.
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest: each Injury destroys an Egg; missed Egg Melee has neither Contamination nor Wound; successful Egg Melee is explicitly unresolved; Grenade/Molotov and Fire effects; Noise after each attempt; no Eggs means Nest destroyed.

answers.answer: 1) Enter through the Evacuation Section A/B Room Action, paying 2 Action cards; the Pod must be Unlocked and have a free Character space in that Section. 2) Make a Noise roll first; entry fails if an Intruder appears or is present, and the Room Action reference also says entry fails if a Malfunction token is in the Evacuation Section Room. 3) A Pod holds up to 2 Characters; Heavy Objects do not take Character spaces. 4) After entering, launch immediately or wait. While waiting, launch at the start of your first round in each Player Phase, or exit voluntarily for free back into the Section Room. If you do not launch in your round, automatically pass. 5) If an Intruder appears in the Section Room while you wait, all Characters in its Pods return to the Room. A second Character boarding a waiting Pod may immediately launch it with the first occupant aboard.
answers.evidence: Escape Pods and Player Reference, Evacuation Section A/B: Room Action cost, unlocked/free space, Noise roll, Intruder/Malfunction restriction, capacity, waiting/launch/exit and consequences.

answers.answer: 1) Victory Check order: Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, then Objectives. 2) If two Engines show Damaged, the ship explodes and everything aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders; launched Pods are already away. 3) If the destination is not Earth, hibernating Characters die; the ship and Intruders survive. Exception: a Character with the Quarantine Objective survives hibernation if destination is Mars. 4) Each surviving hibernating or evacuated Character undergoes the Contamination check: scan cards in deck, discard pile, and hand; if at least one is Infected, shuffle all cards and draw four, and any Contamination card among those four kills. A Larva triggers the shuffle-and-draw-four directly, skipping the initial Scan. 5) Yes, Pod passengers (evacuated survivors) need Contamination checks.
answers.evidence: Victory Check: explicit Engines → Coordinates → Contamination → Objective order; engine and non-Earth outcomes; Quarantine/Mars exception; Contamination check applies to each surviving Character, hibernating or evacuated.
